## docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/manifest.toml
> Standing authorization: one signature pre-authorizes a class of routine work, so each change costs only its acceptance
- OW-WAR-0142 · warrant · authorized · Standing authorization: one signature pre-authorizes a class of routine work, so each change costs only its acceptance · docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/manifest.toml:1

## docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/questions/Q-001.toml
> -
- OW-WAR-0142/Q-001 · question · - · How is routine work authorized? A: a standing authorization. You sign one class (paths, basic assurance, named gates, a budget, an expiry and a count), and each Warrant inside it is authorized from that signature, with its own immutable record naming you. Routine change cost: 0 acts before work, one line in a batched resolution after it. Needs an additive SAS 1.2.0 (§28.8, a clause in §37.5, one §106 row); §27.2 does not change. B: no standing authorization, only batching and presets. Cost: 2 batches per round, and every change waits for your authorize batch before it starts. C: a SAS revision of §27.2 so routine work needs no authorization, with the same per-change cost as A, but the invariant that every authorized Warrant has a human authorizer is dropped. OW-ADR-0029 has the full comparison. Answer A, B or C. · docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/questions/Q-001.toml:1

## docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/questions/Q-002.toml
> -
- OW-WAR-0142/Q-002 · question · - · Under A, what bounds does a class carry by default? The draft proposes an expiry of at most 90 days from signing, at most 50 covered Warrants, and a ceiling of 24000 budget_tokens and 1800 wall_time_seconds per stage. Answer with the numbers, or 'as drafted'. · docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/questions/Q-002.toml:1

## docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/questions/Q-003.toml
> -
- OW-WAR-0142/Q-003 · question · - · Under A, may a covered (routine) Warrant take ownership of a path whose current owner is an authorized but unresolved Warrant? OW-ADR-0021 would let the later authorization own it. Answer 'refuse' or 'allow'. · docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0142/questions/Q-003.toml:1

## docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0148/questions/Q-001.toml
> -
- OW-WAR-0148/Q-001 · question · - · SAS RQ-061 says Liminal owns document semantics and Basis, and RQ-064 says OpenWarrant does not duplicate those kernels. A standalone compiler owning typed document semantics contradicts both as written. (A) a SAS revision, proposed with OW-ADR-0031, moves document semantics for OpenWarrant's own records into its compiler, keeping Liminal's role for documents Liminal holds; or (B) this lands as a projection layer beside Liminal and RQ-061/RQ-064 stand unchanged? · docs/warrants/OW-WAR-0148/questions/Q-001.toml:1
